Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment A moderate thermal day with a few strong cores, but increasing westerly flow in the afternoon brings gusty conditions and cross-wind to several sites. Cloud cover 60–70% with no overdevelopment, and sharp lapse rates at multiple sites require advanced pilot caution.

Site Breakdown

  • Kingsbury grade: Marginal — shifting winds, only briefly aligned around noon, then strong westerly after 3pm. Window 10am–2pm, peak w* 292 ft/min, ceiling 3165 ft AGL. Sharp thermal caution (lapse rate 8.1 °C/km).
  • Hallelujah: Favorable — light winds turn on-ridge by early afternoon, good thermal strength. Window 11am–5pm, peak w* 291 ft/min, ceiling 3414 ft AGL. Sharp thermal caution (lapse rate 9.3 °C/km). Evening soaring possible until 7pm with light NW.
  • Slide Mountain: Unfavorable — winds remain cross to the preferred direction all day, with hazardous low-level speed shear and increasing speeds in the afternoon. Brief thermal window 9am–1pm, peak w* 212 ft/min, ceiling 1397 ft AGL.
  • McClellan: Marginal — decent thermals but low-level speed shear (5 mph/layer) and high bulk shear. Window 10am–3pm, peak w* 344 ft/min, ceiling 3288 ft AGL.
  • West McClellan: Favorable — wind becomes on-ridge from 1pm and thermals cooperate. Window 1pm–4pm, peak w* 286 ft/min, ceiling 2774 ft AGL.
  • Peavine Mountain: Unfavorable — strong, gusty crosswinds (17–27 mph) all day with only brief on-direction window at 10am. Peak w* 305 ft/min, ceiling 2435 ft AGL.
  • Rainbow Ridge: Marginal — mostly light but off-direction winds; low-level speed shear (5 mph/layer) and sharp lapse rate present. Window 10am–4pm, peak w* 294 ft/min, ceiling 4099 ft AGL. Sharp thermal caution (lapse rate 9.3 °C/km).
  • Duck Hill: Marginal — hazardous low-level speed shear (7 mph/layer) and sharp lapse rate. Thermal window 10:30am–3pm, peak w* 305 ft/min, ceiling 3815 ft AGL. Sharp thermal caution (lapse rate 8.7 °C/km). Evening ridge-soar potential after 8pm with light NW flow.
  • Daydreams: Favorable — reliable all-day thermal lift and on-ridge winds from midday onward. Window 11am–7pm (thermals persist into evening), peak w* 211 ft/min, ceiling 2366 ft AGL.

Hazards

  • Sharp thermals — lapse rate >8 °C/km at Kingsbury, Hallelujah, Rainbow Ridge and Duck Hill; stronger, punchier cores suitable for advanced pilots only.
  • Low-level wind shear — hazardous speed shear (≥5 mph/layer) at Slide Mountain, McClellan, Rainbow Ridge and Duck Hill.
  • Rotor/lee turbulence — afternoon westerly surge (15–28 mph at exposed sites) may generate rotor downwind of Peavine Mountain and Carson Range ridgelines.

Site Forecast ?Top of Thermals (PBLH) — height of the turbulent mixing layer; thermals typically reach this ceiling.
LCL (Lifted Condensation Level) — altitude where rising air reaches its dew point; theoretical cloud base.
Cloud Base — lowest model level with >10% cloud fraction.
w* — convective velocity scale; higher = stronger thermals (ft/min).
Cloud Cover — max cloud fraction over the column (0–100%).
